newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed easier on fund selling. December ended $1.20 weaker at $327.50 a tonne, while March fell $1.60 to $324.20. Traders said they were still awaiting the result of Syria's tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of whites and 13,000 tonnes of raws for October and November.
In New York raw sugar futures remained on a downward path. While today's losses were said to be technical, fundamentals remain a bearish background factor.

Higher crops in Brazil, Thailand, South Africa and the absence of China as a large buyer undermined sentiment. Premiums for Thai raw sugar for shipment in the March/May period of 1997 are falling and China is not expected to buy sugar until at least next April.

The Chinese sugar industry is suffering from low internal prices and the government repeatedly said that it will not import to shore up domestic prices. Trade sources said Chinese authorities are unlikely to issue sugar import licences until domestic prices recover to around 5,000 yuan ($602). Sugar prices in Shanghai are currently at around 4,300 yuan ($518) a tonne and they are lower in producing areas.

It was added that prices in Beijing and in Nanning, capital of Guangxi province, were also 4,300 per tonne. Moreover, the country is expected to have a good crop in 1996/97, which will not remain without an effect on imports.

The country imported roughly 2.0 million tonnes of sugar, raw value, in 1995/96 (September/August) down from 2.907 million tonnes imported in 1994/95. Exports in 1995/96 reached 857,000 tonnes, up from 540,000 tonnes last year but down on the 1.102 million tonnes exported in 1993/94.

BRAZIL - Sugar exports continue to develop rather sluggishly. Total exports in August 1996 amounted to 705,900 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 1.04 million tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1996/97 (May/August) up to 1.93 million tonnes, down from 2.35 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 hit the record high of 5.92 million tonnes compared to 4.35 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in May/August 1996 were Nigeria with 284,940 tonnes whites against 114,750 tonnes, the Philippines with 161,122 tonnes against nil, Russia with 141,935 tonnes compared to 300,776 tonnes and the USA with 104,513 tonnes raws compared to 26,855 tonnes.
As Brazil is heading for a record sugar crop it can be expected that shipments will pick up later this year.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG - Sugar imports in May 1996 amounted to 44,413 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 74,107 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first eight months of 1995/96 (October/May) up to 614,507 tonnes compared to 825,035 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 1.14 million tonnes against 663,985 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in October/May 1995/96 were France with 496,243 tonnes whites compared to 732,157 tonnes, the Netherlands with 60,198 tonnes against 11,401 tonnes and Germany with 50,324 tonnes, down from 70,147 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1996 amounted to 64,963 tonnes, down from last year's 203,542 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/May 1995/96 up to 836,291 tonnes against 1.15 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.57 million tonnes against 1.34 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/May 1995/96 were Syria with 141,301 tonnes whites against 112,376 tonnes, Israel with 105,038 tonnes compared to 78,478 tonnes and Turkey with 101,848 tonnes against 57,252 tonnes.
